holidays.name: National Gingerbread House Day
holidays.description: A sweet day for building, decorating, and shamelessly nibbling the roof off a candy-covered cottage. Gumdrops, icing, and structural engineering collide in the name of holiday cheer.
holidays.origin: Gingerbread houses trace back to 16th-century Germany, and the tradition boomed after the Brothers Grimm published Hansel and Gretel in the early 1800s. The day is an unofficial food observance celebrated by bakers and candy lovers.
holidays.funFact: Queen Elizabeth I reportedly had gingerbread cookies made in the likeness of visiting dignitaries.

holidays.name: National Ambrosia Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the retro fluffy dessert salad made of fruit, marshmallows, coconut, and whipped topping or sour cream. It is a potluck classic that divides families between lovers and skeptics.
holidays.origin: The name comes from Greek mythology, where ambrosia was the food of the gods. The American dessert became popular in the late 1800s, when citrus and coconut became more widely available, and the day is a food-calendar observance.
holidays.funFact: Early American ambrosia recipes were just layers of orange slices and fresh coconut, and marshmallows only showed up later.

holidays.name: Poinsettia Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the festive red-leafed plant that fills homes and stores every December. Many people celebrate by buying a poinsettia and trying to keep it alive past New Year's.
holidays.origin: The day marks the anniversary of the death of Joel Roberts Poinsett, the first U.S. Ambassador to Mexico, who introduced the plant to the United States in 1828. He died on December 12, 1851.
holidays.funFact: The bright red parts are not flowers but colored leaves called bracts, and the actual flowers are the tiny yellow bits in the center.

holidays.name: Jamhuri Day
holidays.description: Kenya's national holiday marks the country becoming a republic, with parades, feasts, speeches, and family gatherings. It is a day of national pride and community celebration.
holidays.origin: Kenya gained independence from Britain on December 12, 1963, and became a republic exactly one year later, on December 12, 1964. Jamhuri means republic in Swahili.
holidays.funFact: Kenya's independence and republic anniversaries fall on the same date, so the day is often celebrated alongside Independence Day.

holidays.name: Day of Our Lady of Guadalupe
holidays.description: A vibrant religious and cultural celebration in Mexico with pilgrimages, music, dancing, flowers, and traditional foods. Millions flock to the Basilica of Guadalupe in Mexico City.
holidays.origin: The feast commemorates the 1531 apparitions of the Virgin Mary to Juan Diego on Tepeyac Hill, according to Catholic tradition.
holidays.funFact: The Basilica of Guadalupe is among the most visited Catholic pilgrimage sites in the world.
